deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft, dated [No]vember 1859 (the month the Prime Number paper appeared in the Monatsberichte), of the symmetric integral for xi(s) that appears in the published paper as xi(t)=4∫_1^∞ d(x^{3/2}ψ'(x))/dx · x^{-1/4} cos(½ t log x) dx. Here everything is written in Jacobi's elliptic-function variables: theta_3(q)=Σ_{n∈Z} q^{n^2}=sqrt(2K/π), with q=exp(-πK'/K), K=K(k), K'=K(k'), k'^2=1-k^2.

(1) ζ(s)=Σn^{-s}=Π_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1}. Also ∫_0^∞ e^{-n^2 x} x^{s/2-1}dx = Γ(s/2)/n^s. (Here Π(s/2-1)=Γ(s/2); note there is no π in the exponent on this page.)

(2) Put u=-log q, so Σ_{n≥1} e^{-n^2u} = (θ-1)/2 with θ=sqrt(2K/π). Then Γ(s/2)ζ(s)=∫_0^∞ (θ-1)/2 · u^{s/2-1} du. The transcription drops the ζ(s) on the left.

(3) Integration by parts, using d/du=-d/dlog q (filled in by me): Γ(s/2)ζ(s) = (1/s)∫_0^∞ (dθ/dlog q) u^{s/2} du. The boundary terms vanish for Re s>1, because θ-1 ~ sqrt(π/u) as u→0.

(4) Write u^{s/2}=u^{3/2}·u^{(s-3)/2} and integrate by parts again: Γ(s/2)ζ(s) = (1/s)(2/(s-1))∫_0^∞ [d(u^{3/2} dθ/dlog q)/dlog q] u^{(s-1)/2} du. The boundary terms vanish because u^{3/2}θ' stays bounded as u→0. The aim is to make the integrand invariant under q↔q' (k↔k').

(5) Elliptic auxiliaries.
- Legendre relation in Wronskian form: k(1-k^2)(K dK'/dk - K' dK/dk) = -π/2.
- Since log q=-πK'/K, this gives k'^2 dlog q/dlog k = π^2/(2K^2).
- Hence dlog k/dlog q = 2(k'K/π)^2.
- Hence dlog k'/dlog q = -2(kK/π)^2.

(6) Using u^{3/2}=(πK'/K)^{3/2}: u^{3/2} dθ/dlog q = sqrt(2/π)·½K^{-1/2}(dK/dlog k)·2(k'K/π)^2·(πK'/K)^{3/2} = sqrt2 · k'^2 (dK/dlog k) K'^{3/2}/π. All powers of K cancel.

(7) The Legendre differential equation is d(k k'^2 dK/dk)/dk = kK. Equivalently d(k'^2 dK/dlog k)/dlog k = k^2 K.

(8) Differentiate (6) with respect to log q:
F := d(u^{3/2}θ')/dlog q = sqrt2 (k^2K/π) K'^{3/2}·2(k'K/π)^2 + sqrt2 (k'^2/π)(dK/dlog k)(3/2)K'^{1/2}(dK'/dlog k')·(-2)(kK/π)^2.
Simplifying (mine): F = (2sqrt2/π^3) k^2k'^2 K^3 K'^{3/2} [1 - (3/2)(dlogK/dlogk)(dlogK'/dlogk')]. The bracket can equally be written as on the page, with dlogK/dlogk' · dlogK'/dlogk; the two products are identical.

(9) Change variable to v=log(K'/K), which runs over (-∞,∞). Then u=πe^v and u^{(s-1)/2}du = π^{(s+1)/2}(K'/K)^{(s+1)/2} dv. Combining, and using K^3K'^{3/2}(K'/K)^{(s+1)/2} = (KK')^{9/4}(K'/K)^{s/2-1/4}, gives
π^{-s/2}Γ(s/2)ζ(s) = (π^2/(4s(s-1))) ∫_{-∞}^{∞} k^2k'^2 (4KK'/π^2)^{9/4} [1-(3/2)(dlogK/dlogk')(dlogK'/dlogk)] (K'/K)^{s/2-1/4} dlog(K'/K).

(10) Purpose. Everything except (K'/K)^{s/2-1/4} is symmetric under k↔k', which sends v→-v. So with s=½+ti the integral is an even (cosine) transform. This gives the functional equation ξ(s)=ξ(1-s) and the real cosine-integral for ξ(t) of the 1859 paper, with the kernel expressed through elliptic integrals.
errors: Line 2 as transcribed lacks ζ(s) on the left. It should read Π(s/2-1)ζ(s) = ∫... (possibly a transcription loss rather than Riemann's slip).

The auxiliary relation is transcribed as kk' ∂log q/∂log k = ππ/(2KK). The correct relation is k'k' ∂log q/∂log k = ππ/(2KK). The consequences Riemann writes next (∂log k/∂log q = 2(k'K/π)^2 and ∂log k'/∂log q = -2(kK/π)^2) are correct, so this is likely a misreading or a pen slip.

Constant in the final line. With the base (KK'/ππ)^{9/4}, the correct prefactor is 4·sqrt2·π^2/(s(s-1)), not π^2/(4s(s-1)). The page's π^2/(4s(s-1)) is exactly right with the base (4KK'/ππ)^{9/4}, since 4^{9/4}=16sqrt2. That is the version the transcription shows as struck (and the symmetric form used on the previous page). So either the deletion was itself the slip, or the transcription misread an overwrite.
The previous page has a variant (2+3 ∂logK/∂logk' ∂logK'/∂logk) with a factor ∂K'/∂log k. This page corrects it to 1-(3/2)(...) with ∂K'/∂log k'; the version here is the correct one.

Unstated: boundary terms in both integrations by parts vanish only for Re s>1. The final formula then extends to all s by analytic continuation, since the kernel decays like exp(-c·e^{|v|}). Riemann leaves this implicit, as in the published paper.

results.what: Mellin transform of the theta function, Γ(s/2)ζ(s)=∫_0^∞ψ(u)u^{s/2-1}du, with θ_3=sqrt(2K/π)
results.modern_name: Riemann's theta-function proof of the functional equation

results.what: Double integration by parts giving ξ as a Mellin transform of d(x^{3/2}ψ'(x))/dx, symmetric under s↔1-s
results.modern_name: Riemann's integral representation of ξ(t) (kernel Φ(u) of Pólya / de Bruijn–Newman)

results.what: Legendre relation in Wronskian form; dlog k/dlog q=2(k'K/π)^2; Legendre ODE d(kk'^2K')/dk=kK
results.modern_name: Legendre's relation / hypergeometric ODE for complete elliptic integrals; Jacobi's nome derivative

results.what: Explicit expression of the ξ-kernel through k, K, K': k^2k'^2(4KK'/π^2)^{9/4}[1-(3/2)(dlogK/dlogk)(dlogK'/dlogk')], integrated against (K'/K)^{s/2-1/4} dlog(K'/K)
results.modern_name: Modular-form expression of the Riemann ξ kernel (theta-function derivatives via elliptic moduli)
results.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution; an elliptic-function rewriting of Riemann's own kernel

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the symmetric ξ-integral in Riemann's 1859 paper; he explicitly cites Jacobi's Fundamenta there, so the use of theta/elliptic functions is expected. The only non-published feature is writing the kernel d(x^{3/2}ψ')/dx in closed elliptic-modulus form. That is a nice but minor unpublished detail, partly visible already in known Nachlass descriptions.
